title: Verifier-Gated LLM NetOps: A Confirmatory Evaluation of Input-Sanitization and Deterministic Verification Against Adversarial Intents
abstract: We report a preregistered, confirmatory study of defenses for LLM-driven network-configuration generation under adversarially crafted intents. Following a frozen preregistration (study cand-2026-03), we executed a paired experiment (Nplanned=150 adversarial intents; Npairs_included=141) using a single-model pipeline (gpt-5-mini) and a deterministic CLI validator. Conditions compared the baseline LLM-only pipeline to a guarded pipeline combining template-based input sanitization with deterministic verifier-gating (automatic rejection of any configuration failing safety checks). Primary outcome: paired acceptance-for-deployment of unsafe/violating configurations. Results: baseline accepted 135/141 (95.74%); guarded accepted 141/141 (100%); paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.04255; exact McNemar two-sided p = 0.03125; 95% bootstrap CI [0.01418, 0.07801]. Confirmatory hypothesis H1 (guarded reduces accepted unsafe configs vs baseline) is supported under the preregistered estimand and handling of technical failures. Findings are limited to the synthetic intent templates, single-model evaluation, and the deterministic validator implementation; we discuss construct and external-validity threats and provide machine-verifiable execution artifacts and hashes in the archived bundle.

sections.introduction: Large language models (LLMs) promise to simplify network operations by translating operator intent into device configurations, but they also produce safety- and correctness-critical failures (hallucination, malformed CLI, semantic violations, and prompt-injection) that can create operational risk. Prior work has shown that combining generative models with deterministic verifiers can materially reduce errors in prototype NetOps tasks. We ask a focused, preregistered research question: How effective are template-based input sanitization plus deterministic verifier-gating at preventing adversarially crafted intents from producing unsafe or policy-violating network configurations in an LLM-driven NetOps pipeline? Contributions. (1) A preregistered confirmatory experiment (cand-2026-03) that evaluates verifier-gating and sanitization against adversarial intents under a paired design. (2) A reproducible execution bundle and deterministic analysis showing a statistically detectable reduction in accepted unsafe outputs when guarded defenses are applied (paired difference = 0.04255, p=0.03125). (3) An explicit discussion of operational implications, failure diagnostics, and threats to validity.
sections.related_work: Deterministic network verification frameworks such as Header Space Analysis and incremental checkers (NetPlumber/VeriFlow) provide rapid, formal checks of forwarding and configuration invariants and are natural validators for generate–validate pipelines [1],[2]. Recent NetOps studies demonstrate that LLMs alone produce promising drafts but commit topology, syntax, and semantic errors; supplementing generation with localized verifier feedback improves outcomes in prototype tasks [3]. Benchmarks and surveys (NetConfEval and LLM-for-AIOps surveys) document rising interest in LLMs for configuration tasks and call for operationally meaningful evaluation metrics beyond text-match accuracy [4],[5]. Security analyses of LLM-integrated systems highlight prompt-injection and indirect prompt attacks as realistic threats that can subvert intended behavior, motivating sanitization and gating defenses [6]. Work on tool-augmented LMs (e.g., Toolformer) shows the practical value of training or orchestrating models to call external tools during generation [7]. (References mapped to cited_record_ids.)
sections.methodology: Preregistration and design. The experiment was preregistered (study_id cand-2026-03; preregistration SHA-256: ba6ed25e84c7240fbe94f2d50b3e778fbfffd810ff2db632df8946e85f0f1373) before observing outcomes. Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline (proportion accepted for deployment under guarded minus baseline). Design: paired binary comparison on adversarial intents (N=150 planned). Sampling unit: adversarial intent; each intent was run under both conditions. Generation semantics: shared_initial_candidate (the same initial LLM candidate seed was shared across baseline and guarded conditions when applicable per preregistration). Interventions. Baseline: single-shot LLM generation (gpt-5-mini) from an intent template, scored by deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Guarded: template-based input sanitization followed by LLM generation plus deterministic verifier-gating that blocks any candidate failing the validator. A single automated repair call was permitted by preregistration only when the frozen repair policy allowed it. Models, tools, and automation. Model: gpt-5-mini (provider: openai_responses). Validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (scorer_id). Task generator: deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 producing synthetic intent templates covering ACLs, interface admin, MTU, VLAN, and safe-change workflow constraints. Execution contract and failure treatment. Planned episodes: 150 intents × 2 conditions = 300 episodes; completed episodes = 282; complete_pairs included = 141 (pairs where at least one run succeeded). Technical failures (model API failure, verifier timeout, parser error) were logged and handled per the preregistered missingness plan (paired exclusion when both runs failed; sensitivity analyses treating failures as attack-failed). All runtime artifacts, provider calls, and hashes were recorded in the archived execution manifest.
sections.results: Execution summary. Planned episodes=300; completed episodes=282; failed episodes=18; model_calls_used=156. Primary (confirmatory) analysis used the 141 complete pairs. Observed outcomes (complete_pairs=141): baseline_successes=135 (135/141 = 0.9574468), guarded_successes=141 (141/141 = 1.0). Contingency cell counts: n11 (both accepted)=135; n10 (guarded=1, baseline=0)=6; n01 (guarded=0, baseline=1)=0; n00=0. Paired test. Exact McNemar two-sided test: p = 0.03125. Point estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.04255319148936165. Bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed=1729): [0.014184397163120567, 0.07801418439716312]. Interpretation. Under the preregistered estimand and exclusion rules, the guarded pipeline produced a small but statistically detectable increase in the per-intent acceptance outcome (all guarded pairs were accepted while six pairs were rejected under baseline). Exploratory diagnostics. The six discordant intents where guarded succeeded but baseline did not are consistent with sanitizer-or-repair-mediated corrections (the validator traces and provider-call logs show repair-stage activity in a subset of runs; repair_applied flags and provider traces are available in the archived artifacts). Missingness and robustness. Both-missing pairs = 9 (18 failed episodes total: 9 baseline-only failures and 9 guarded-only failures distributed across episodes); sensitivity analyses treating missing generative outputs as failures are provided in the archive; they do not overturn the primary qualitative conclusion but reduce effective N and widen CIs (see archived analysis files). All per-condition counts, contingency table, and analysis artifacts are in the execution bundle (hashes in the manifest).
sections.discussion: What the confirmatory result means. In this synthetic but preregistered pipeline, template-based input sanitization combined with deterministic verifier-gating eliminated accepted unsafe outputs among included pairs and produced a small but statistically detectable improvement over the LLM-only baseline. Operational implication: integrating a deterministic validator as an enforceable gate materially reduces the risk that adversarially crafted intents produce configurations that would be accepted for deployment in this controlled setting. Caveats and limits. Construct validity: the deterministic validator operationalizes a limited set of safety properties (CLI grammar, required sequence constraints, protected-interface invariants). It does not capture every operational risk (vendor-specific semantics, complex protocol interactions, runtime state beyond the modeled device state). External validity: the experiment used a single model (gpt-5-mini), a synthetic task bank (intent templates), and a single validator implementation; results do not establish production-ready generality across vendors, protocols (BGP/MPLS), or large topologies. Internal validity: the paired design and preregistered missingness rules protect against some biases, but 18 technical failures and the exclusion rule (exclude pair if both runs failed) reduce effective sample size. Security implications. The study addresses only a restricted adversarial model (mutations of synthetic intents); prompt-injection and indirect-injection threats in richer retrieval-augmented or multi-source settings remain important open problems. Recommendations. Practitioners should pair LLM-based generators with deterministic verifiers and conservative gating; additionally, invest in validator coverage for protocol-level semantics and multi-vendor CLIs and in defenses against prompt-injection at inputs and retrieval boundaries.
sections.conclusion: We present a preregistered confirmatory evaluation showing that combining template-based input sanitization with deterministic verifier-gating reduced the acceptance of unsafe, adversarially induced configurations in a synthetic LLM-driven NetOps pipeline (paired difference ≈ 4.25 percentage points; p=0.03125). The result supports the practical value of verifier-gated architectures for mitigating some classes of LLM failure in NetOps, but important limitations (synthetic tasks, single model, validator coverage) constrain generalization. Future work should expand validator semantics, diversify models and vendors, and evaluate defenses against more sophisticated prompt-injection and retrieval-based attacks. All execution artifacts, analysis files, and hashes are archived in the supplied evidence bundle for reproducibility.

The exact initial prompting strategy, tool-call traces, model responses, validator traces, and analysis artifacts are archived in the execution bundle referenced in the manuscript evidence. The archived bundle contains machine-verifiable artifacts (execution manifest, analysis results, and hashes) necessary to reproduce analyses; embargo and contamination policies described in the preregistration were followed for any flagged high-risk artifacts.
limitations: Synthetic task bank and intent templates — not real production traffic or operator logs; results may not generalize to field datasets.
Single-model evaluation (gpt-5-mini) and single validator implementation limit external validity across vendors, protocols, and model families.
Validator coverage constrained to encoded safety properties (CLI grammar, required sequences, protected-interface invariants); some protocol-level or dynamic runtime semantics are not represented.
Technical failures (18/300 episodes) reduced effective sample size; paired exclusion (both-run failures) was preregistered and applied.
Adversary model limited to mutations of synthetic intents; prompt-injection in retrieval-augmented or multi-source pipelines was not exhaustively evaluated here.
